sections.heading: C2 — Vehicle checks and equipment
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Vehicle checks and equipment

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
When headlamps are required, a vehicle stopped or parked on a roadway must show parking lights that are white or amber ahead and red behind, visible for 500 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A01
Motor vehicles require a front windshield, with safety glass required for those manufactured after January 1, 1956. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A01
The windshield must stay in a condition that does not block the driver’s view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
Do not attach material to any window if it restricts the driver’s view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A01
Working windshield wipers are required to remove rain, snow and other moisture. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A02
Vehicles manufactured between January 1, 1965 and January 1, 1968 must have belts for both outer front seats. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A02
Vehicles manufactured after January 1, 1968 require seatbelts at every designated seating position. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A02
Seatbelts must be kept in working order. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A02
A driver may not drive in Montana unless each occupant has a properly adjusted and fastened safety belt. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A02
For buses and trucks over 80 inches wide, and trailers or semitrailers over 3,000 pounds gross vehicle weight and over that width, two clearance lamps are required at the front and two at the rear, one on each side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A02
A truck tractor needs two front clearance lamps, one on each side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A02
A pole trailer above 3,000 pounds gross vehicle weight needs a clearance lamp on each side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A02
Vehicles made after January 1, 1956 need two rear taillamps, except motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, quadricycles and truck tractors. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A02
Clearance lamps must be amber at the front or side and red at the rear, and visible for 500 feet when required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A02
A load projecting at least four feet beyond the vehicle body needs a red lamp at its farthest rear point, visible for 500 feet, while headlamps are required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A02
When headlamps are not required, a load extending four feet or more beyond the vehicle body needs a red flag at least 12 inches square. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A02
A farm tractor or implement of husbandry moving on a highway during required-headlamp hours must show a front white light visible for at least 500 feet and a rear red light visible for 500 feet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A02
Required farm-vehicle lights must be mounted to show the vehicle’s farthest left projection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A02
A vehicle may carry no more than two spot or auxiliary fog lamps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A02
Turn spot lamps off when approaching another moving vehicle from either direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A02
Fog lamps may accompany low-beam headlights only if the fog-lamp beam is no stronger than the low beam. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A03
Trailers, semitrailers and pole trailers need separation-activated break-away brakes if they have air or vacuum brakes or weigh more than 3,000 pounds gross. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R23 | anchor: A03
Maintain brakes in working order and adjust them to act equally on all wheels. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R24 | anchor: A03
Vehicle sirens, whistles and bells are prohibited except where authorized emergency vehicles are permitted to use them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R25 | anchor: A03
A trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer weighing 3,000 pounds gross vehicle weight or less needs a securely fastened front steel safety chain or cable at least one-quarter inch in diameter. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R26 | anchor: A03
A truck with at least one-ton capacity, passenger bus or truck tractor must carry the specified warning equipment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R27 | anchor: A03
Three emergency reflective triangles meeting United States Department of Transportation Motor Vehicles Safety Standard 125 may replace the listed warning-device set. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R28 | anchor: A03
Vehicles carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases, or using compressed gas fuel, must not carry flame-producing warning devices. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R29 | anchor: A04
If a truck, passenger bus, tractor, trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer is disabled on a highway or shoulder while lamps are required, place an initial warning device immediately on the traffic side toward approaching traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R30 | anchor: A04
For the listed disabled vehicles on an undivided highway during required-lamp hours, warning devices go 100 feet behind and 100 feet ahead in the occupied lane, plus a traffic-side device at least 10 feet toward the nearest approaching traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R31 | anchor: A04
For the listed disabled vehicles on a divided highway during required-lamp hours, use the 200-foot rear placement and place the other lane device 100 feet in the same direction instead of in front. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R32 | anchor: A04
When a listed disabled vehicle is within 500 feet of a curve, hill or other blocked view, put the warning in that direction at least 500 feet from the vehicle so approaching traffic has adequate warning. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R33 | anchor: A04
When the stated lamp-time warning-device requirement does not apply to a listed disabled vehicle on a roadway, the driver must display two red flags at the specified front and rear positions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R34 | anchor: A04
In the stated highway or shoulder disablement situations, a vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquid or compressed gas, or using compressed gas fuel, needs immediate red electric-lantern or portable-red-reflector warnings on its traffic side and 100 feet ahead and behind in its occupied lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R35 | anchor: A04
Do not use flares, fuses or other flame signals to warn of a disabled vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases, or using compressed gas as fuel. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R36 | anchor: A04
A slow-moving vehicle or item of equipment, animal-drawn vehicle, or road-work machine normally operating at 25 miles per hour or less needs the rear emblem, except machinery doing actual road work while protected by a flagger or warning signs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R37 | anchor: A04
The slow-moving emblem is a fluorescent yellow-orange triangle with a 14-inch base and 14-inch height. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R38 | anchor: A04
The slow-moving emblem needs reflective red border stripes one and three-quarter inches wide. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R39 | anchor: A04
Mount the slow-moving emblem at the rear center, three to five feet above the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R40 | anchor: A04
On a two-lane road, a slow vehicle that leaves no clear passing lane must pull over at the first safe opportunity with sufficient turnout space to let others pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R41 | anchor: A04
Keep the windshield clean because sunlight or headlights on dirty glass can make seeing difficult. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R42 | anchor: A04
Keep washer fluid filled and use antifreeze washer fluid where temperatures may drop below freezing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R43 | anchor: A04
Clean interior window surfaces, especially when smoking has left a film. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R44 | anchor: A04
Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost from the front, side and rear windows. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]
